## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: the new twelve-character minimum is not applied everywhere. The pull request description says the change raises "the minimum in the password validators", but the third validator, `app/invite.py`, still accepts 8-character passwords. This review read all three `accepts_password` validators and their tests; it did not run them. One strength: the updated reset and signup tests check the exact boundary (11 rejected, 12 accepted), so they would fail if either constant reverted.

## Changes
The pull request raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` from 8 to 12 in `app/reset.py` and `app/signup.py` and updates their boundary tests to 0, 8, 11, 12 and 13. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — Raise the invite validator minimum to twelve — A user who sets a password through the invite flow can still choose one of 8 to 11 characters, because `app/invite.py:1` still says `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`, and only reset and signup were changed to 12. The pull request body says "Our security policy now requires passwords of at least twelve characters. This raises the minimum in the password validators", and `app/invite.py:4-5` is the third copy of the same `accepts_password` validator. `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts `length >= 8`, so the tests do not catch the gap. — Invited users can create passwords that break the stated twelve-character security policy, and the invite tests treat that as correct. — Fix: Set `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` to the same `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` boundaries. Alternatively, define the constant in one shared place so the three validators cannot drift apart.
